take.en: Open-source OrbStack-class runtime for Mac — drop-in Docker plus Firecracker microVMs so coding agents run with a real kernel boundary, not hope and allowlists.

why.en: Founders still hand Claude Code and friends the whole laptop, or they rent brittle cloud sandboxes. ArcBox makes isolation the default on the machine you already use: disposable microVMs with their own kernel, filesystem, and network, while still speaking Docker for everyday containers.

explanation.en: ArcBox is a pure-Rust container and VM runtime aimed at macOS as an open alternative to Docker Desktop and OrbStack. One daemon covers four workload tiers: Docker-compatible containers (and local k3s), agent sandboxes, full Linux machines, and throwaway macOS guests. Sandboxes boot nested Firecracker microVMs inside the guest — each agent gets a real isolation boundary instead of a process jail. Public beta under MIT/Apache-2.0, with a CLI (`abctl`), desktop app, gRPC sandbox API, and a path to pool your own hardware as fleet capacity.

howItWorks.en: Install via Homebrew cask or the get.arcbox.dev script, start the daemon, then `abctl docker enable` so existing Docker CLI and Compose keep working. For agents: set your API key and run `abctl claude` — it builds a sandbox template, attaches your terminal inside Claude Code, and can skip host permission prompts because the microVM is the wall. Or create sandboxes from images/Dockerfiles, exec, copy files, expose ports, checkpoint and restore. Nested virt needs Apple Silicon M3+ and macOS 15+ on the default VZ backend; other hosts fail fast with a clear error.

different.en: Not another agent harness and not a closed Mac Docker app. The product story is open local infrastructure: OrbStack-level container UX plus first-class agent microVMs and the same sandbox primitive you can scale later — isolation by kernel, not by vibes.

x.en:
ArcBox is the open OrbStack play with a real agent story. drop-in Docker on Mac, plus Firecracker microVMs so Claude Code runs behind a kernel boundary — abctl claude and the host stays clean. isolation as infrastructure, not another allowlist.
